environment.description: Same Tomcat 9.0.62 application deployed on ECS Fargate behind ALB with two specific configurations: (1) The ALB has a listener rule that inspects WebSocket Upgrade requests and enforces a custom header X-WS-Origin-Nonce that is injected by a CloudFront Function on the edge only for requests originating from the registered domain (verified via CloudFront signed cookies with a 5-minute TTL rotation). Without the valid nonce header, the ALB returns 403 before the connection reaches Tomcat. (2) The frontend HTML page that loads the WebSocket client script uses Subresource Integrity with sha384 pinning on the CDN-hosted ws-queue-client.js, and the CSP includes require-sri-for script style (legacy directive) combined with a strict Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self' https://cdn.example.com 'sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8wC'; require-trusted-types-for 'script'. This means even if an attacker compromises the CDN to serve a modified ws-queue-client.js that initiates cross-origin WebSocket connections, the browser will refuse to execute the tampered script because the hash won't match. The combination of ALB nonce validation (preventing direct cross-origin WS connections) and SRI (preventing tampered client-side scripts from being loaded) blocks both the server-side and client-side attack vectors for WebSocket hijacking.

config.load_balancer: ALB with custom listener rule requiring X-WS-Origin-Nonce header
config.cloudfront_function: Injects X-WS-Origin-Nonce from signed cookie validation, 5-min TTL rotation
config.alb_rule: IF header X-WS-Origin-Nonce NOT present OR invalid THEN fixed-response 403
config.sri_enforcement: sha384 integrity attribute on all CDN script tags
config.vpc_endpoint_policy: Restrict sqs:* to specific queue ARN
